jobs.title: Golang Backend Engineer, Financial Product Fraud
jobs.description:
Our Global Structure


Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we're unlocking new possibilities as one global team.

Your job is to make sure every payout and transaction lands with the right person.

We have spent years getting very good at protecting the things a marketplace has always had to protect: checkout fraud, account takeover, courier abuse. But we are no longer only a marketplace. We now issue banking products, lend to merchants, move instant payouts to couriers, and collect cash on the doorstep. Every one of those is a new way for money to leave the platform.

This is a new team, and it owns that surface: fraud wherever money moves through the platform. Who receives it, who lends it, who collects it, and who holds it in a financial account. Think instant payout rails, merchant cash advances, and platform-issued banking and earned-wage products serving millions of couriers and merchants. These are live loss surfaces, and the volume grows with every financial product we launch.

We are now looking for a Backend Engineer (Golang) to build that protection. You will design and ship real-time detection and automated enforcement for our financial products across DoorDash, Wolt, and Deliveroo. The work is high-throughput, low-latency, and unusually consequential: a rule you ship on Monday can stop a serious loss by Friday. It is also close to greenfield, so you will be setting the patterns every future financial product inherits on day one.

This role will be based in London, UK as one of the founding engineering roles in our London hub, working closely with our teams in Helsinki and Berlin.

What you'll do:

  • Build and maintain high-throughput, low-latency backend services in Go that score financial events in real time, including payout enrollments, bank account links, credit applications, and account-to-account transfers.
  • Design fraud detection and automated enforcement for our financial products end to end: from signal collection through to the decision that blocks a fraudulent payout.
  • Build on and extend our shared fraud decisioning platform, so signals, rules, and models work across all three of our brands instead of being rebuilt three times.
  • Partner closely with risk analysts, data scientists, and product managers to turn observed fraud patterns into shipped detection, and to know when a rule, a model, or a product change is the right answer.
  • Work across team boundaries with our account security, payments fraud, and financial product teams. We build on their signals rather than rebuild them, so clean interfaces matter.
  • Contribute to architectural discussions and technical decisions as we establish the fraud infrastructure baseline for financial products, with support from senior engineers on the team.
  • Write well-tested, observable code and help the team hold a high quality bar. In fraud, a silent failure is a loss event.

Our expectations:

  • 3 to 6 years of professional software engineering experience, including backend services you have shipped and owned in production.
  • 1+ years of production experience in Golang, or strong experience in another backend language and real enthusiasm for picking Go up quickly.
  • A working understanding of low-latency, high-throughput distributed systems. Real-time decisioning comes with a latency budget, and you are keen to learn to build inside one.
  • Hands-on experience with SQL and/or NoSQL databases, and some exposure to event-driven architectures (Kafka or similar).
  • Willingness to operate what you build, including a share of on-call, with a pragmatic approach to reliability.
  • Uses AI tooling in day-to-day development and can critically evaluate its output for correctness and quality.

Nice to have

  • Experience in fraud, risk, payments, lending, or financial crime, especially money movement fraud, bank account linking fraud, payout abuse, or lending fraud.
  • Experience with rules engines, real-time feature stores, or ML model serving in a decisioning path.
  • Background in Kotlin, Java, Python, or Node.js alongside Go.
  • Familiarity with cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP).
  • Experience working across multiple brands, regions, or regulatory regimes.

What we value

  • A product-oriented mindset. You think beyond the ticket, understand the "why" behind the work, and take a high level of responsibility for outcomes rather than output.
  • Comfort with ambiguity. This is a new team on a new surface; parts of the charter are still being drawn, and you will help draw them.
  • A track record of owning a project or feature end to end, especially in fast-paced environments.
  • Clear and proactive communication, with a collaborative spirit. We work across three companies and several time zones, so we move fast, but we succeed together.
  • An adversarial instinct. The best fraud engineers enjoy thinking like the attacker.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusion

At Deliveroo, we know that a great workplace reflects the world around us and that true diversity and inclusion make us stronger, more creative, and better at what we do. We're committed to fostering an environment where everyone can do their best work and feel they belong.

We believe in equality of opportunity and welcome candidates from all backgrounds regardless of age, gender, ethnicity, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, socio-economic background, religion, or belief.

If you have a disability or long-term health condition and need support to apply for one of our roles, or require any reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process, you'll have the opportunity to let us know once you've submitted your application. We'll share details on how to request support so we can ensure you have a fair and equitable experience.

If you're excited about making a real impact in a fast-moving marketplace and growing your career alongside ambitious, supportive teams, we'd love to hear from you!

jobs.description:
Notre mission ⚖️

Chez Doctrine, nous construisons le leader de l’IA juridique en Europe.

Notre conviction ? Le droit ne doit pas être ralenti par des tâches répétitives. Il doit être augmenté par une IA spécialisée, conçue pour comprendre, analyser et produire du raisonnement juridique avec un haut niveau d’exigence.

Notre ambition ? Permettre aux professionnels du droit de gagner en fiabilité, en efficacité et en sérénité, grâce à une plateforme unique, exhaustive et sécurisée.

Aujourd’hui, 27 000 professionnels du droit, répartis dans cinq pays (France, Italie, Allemagne, Espagne, Luxembourg), nous font confiance.

Notre développement est guidé par une approche claire : une vision globale, ancrée dans une compréhension fine des spécificités locales.

Derrière cette ambition, une équipe d’environ 250 personnes, réunies autour d’un même objectif : accompagner les juristes et avocats à toutes les étapes de leur travail, de l’analyse à la rédaction.

Et nous n’en sommes qu’au début.


Contexte du stage

 Au sein de l'équipe Fondation (ingénieurs Fullstack et SRE), vous aurez un rôle central pour améliorer l'Expérience Développeur (DX) chez Doctrine : simplifier et sécuriser les processus quotidiens de développement, avec un impact direct sur l'efficacité de toutes les équipes techniques.
  • Conception et spécifications : comprendre et formaliser les besoins avec l'équipe Fondation, puis rédiger le cahier des charges (spécifications techniques et fonctionnelles).
  • Planification itérative : une fois le cahier des charges validé, définir un plan de mise en œuvre par lots, pour des livraisons fréquentes et une visibilité constante sur l'avancement.
Les missions
  • Mission principale : Conception et mise en place d'un outil de validation automatisé dans nos pipelines CircleCI pour vérifier la conformité de notre code d'Infrastructure as Code (IaC) avec nos règles internes, au sein d'une infrastructure récente basée sur AWS et Terraform.
  • Contrôle augmenté par LLM : Intégration de modèles de langage pour analyser les configurations Terraform, repérer les écarts et générer des explications ou des suggestions de correction directement dans les Pull Requests.
  • Industrialisation des règles : Formalisation de nos standards d'infrastructure et automatisation des alertes ou des blocages dans le workflow de build en cas de non-conformité.

Les à-côtés du poste 👁️
Comme tous les ingénieurs de Doctrine, tu participeras au chapter transverse Software Engineering. Il se réunit 2 fois par mois pour :
  • Partager des connaissances : amélioration continue, bonnes pratiques…
  • Proposer des évolutions : nouveaux outils à expérimenter, nouveaux process à mettre en œuvre
  • Support ponctuel : guider les ingénieurs sur leurs besoins liés à l'exploitation
  • Chapter meetings (EIR) : accompagnement dédié si tu souhaites présenter ton projet ou un autre sujet technique
    • Ce qui t'attend chez Doctrine
  • Contribuer à un projet ambitieux, avec un impact réel et positif sur la société : rendre le droit plus accessible et plus ouvert
  • Un accompagnement sur mesure dès ton arrivée pour naviguer vite dans l'écosystème juridique
  • Apprendre sans cesse et partager tes connaissances (talks internes/externes, meetups, Tech & Sales Monthly, blog Medium…)
  • Une équipe en ébullition, avec de la place pour innover et mener des projets en autonomie ou en équipe

    • Une aventure dans laquelle la formation et le partage des connaissances font partis du quotidien.
    • Rejoindre une entreprise avec une vie d’équipe riche et dynamique : conférences, team-buildings, déjeuner, offsite, afterwork, etc.

    Nos valeurs 🤝

    Chez Doctrine, nos 4 valeurs nous accompagnent au quotidien et dans notre ambition de faire bouger les choses.

    • Challenge the status quo : nous défendons les idées audacieuses qui contribuent à l’évolution de tout un secteur.
    • Liberty and responsibility : nous encourageons l’autonomie, l’impact de chacun·e et l’ownership.
    • Knowledge is power : l'information est au cœur de la mission de Doctrine, et nous cherchons constamment à progresser.
    • Release early, release often and listen to your customers : nous croyons au pouvoir de l’itération et à l’importance d’écouter en permanence notre marché, nos client·e·s et leurs problématiques.
     

    Nos avantages pour faire la différence ☀️

    🏡 Une politique de télétravail flexible permettant - selon les équipes - jusqu’à trois jours de télétravail par semaine.

    🌴 Une politique de congés flexibles

    🧘 Un accès gratuit à la plateforme d'accompagnement à la santé mentale Moka.care et un accompagnement individuel allant jusqu’à 6 séances par an

    Notre processus de recrutement 🚀

    • Une rencontre d’1h avec ton/ta futur.e manager, pour détailler le poste et le scope de l’équipe, mais aussi répondre à toutes tes questions.

jobs.title: Operations Strategy Associate
jobs.description:
About Clipboard

Our mission is to uplift as many communities as possible. We do this through our app-based marketplace that connects healthcare professionals with the workplaces that need amazing workers. This enables hundreds of thousands of people to achieve financial stability for themselves and their families while providing essential care to millions of people across the U.S.


Founded in 2016, we are a remote-first team of over 1,000 people building a top Y-Combinator company and have been profitable since 2022. We’re the leader in Long-Term Care staffing and are rapidly expanding into Home Health, Hospitals, and more, meaning we have more work to do than people to do it, and are growing our team to support millions more people and their communities.

 

Overview

The Operations Strategy Associate role is a generalist role at Clipboard suited for the “all-around athlete” type who wants exposure to a range of problems and opportunities.

You’re likely someone who’s interested in and capable of solving different problem types, you’re resourceful, adaptable, and confident you can figure it out if you can sink your teeth in deep enough. These are the ingredients for a problem-solver who is eager to flex into multiple different types of roles and responsibilities depending on what’s needed and most impactful.

While we know that you'll likely start working within one of our Operations teams, we don’t know exactly what work or projects you’ll drive out of the gate, so you’ll notice the work we’re advertising isn’t entirely specific. Some candidates may begin in more execution-focused roles within Operations, depending on their strengths, while others may take on project or team leadership earlier on.

But we’ll make a few promises about the role: it will be high-impact, fast-paced work that directly affects our customers, product, and business.

 

What you’ll Be Doing

  • Analyze operational data to spot trends and bottlenecks, and build dashboards, reports, and models that guide business decisions.

  • Research, evaluate, and implement new technologies, including AI, automations, and internal tools, to make operations more effective.

  • Design processes, workflows, and operating procedures that improve efficiency, quality, and customer experience

  • Lead cross-functional projects and strategic initiatives from planning through execution, partnering with Operations, Product, Engineering, Customer Success, and other teams.

Here are a few projects you might own:

  • Redesign how we reach out to workplaces about switching payment methods, such as moving check-paying customers to eCheck, to speed up cash collection.

  • Research, vet, and onboard a vendor that brings AI agents into our customer-facing operations.

  • Build a predictive model that flags high-risk payers early and accurately, so we can act before payments go overdue.

  • Take over a team of agents within one of our Operations teams and improve its performance, quality, and workflows.

 

What you’ll Need

  • 2+ years of work or internship experience, including but not limited to cross-functional roles such as Strategy/Business/Product Operations, Program Management, Consultancy or Business Analytics.

  • Experience solving operational problems by improving processes, designing workflows, or building scalable systems, while juggling multiple priorities in ambiguous, fast-moving environments.

  • Strong data analysis skills with hands-on experience in SQL, Python, or similar tools.

  • Clear written and verbal communication, with the ability to explain complex problems simply and align stakeholders across teams.

  • A deep curiosity that drives you to reason from first principles and dig until you find the root cause.

  • The habit of rolling up your sleeves and going to the source. You don't just take someone's word for it; you find out for yourself by testing the feature, listening to the agent call, calling the customer, or running the workflow.

 

We are hiring for multiple openings in this role and won’t close the funnel prematurely based on other candidates, but may periodically pause applications due to volume. We hope to welcome everyone who meets our bar for excellence, and we hope that includes you.

 

Why Join Clipboard?

  • We are remote-first, giving you the flexibility to work with us from many places.

  • Fast-paced startup environment. Join a company that values curiosity, independence, and growth.

  • A hiring process that rewards skills, not just experience. Every applicant gets a fair shot, our selection is based on real-world problem-solving ability, not just credentials.

  • Opportunity to make a significant impact with our customers on both sides of the marketplace.

     

Hiring Process

  1. Application

  3. Case Interview(s) with our Operations Leaders

  5. Interview with one of our Co-CEOs

*After submitting your application, please check your spam folder periodically over the next few days for updates.

Clipboard would never ask you for money or your bank details to participate in our hiring process. Report any scammers impersonating the Clipboard hiring team members here.

jobs.title: Data Engineer
jobs.description:
Data Engineer

London (Waterloo) · Full-time · Hybrid, three days per week in the office

Who we are

At GetGround, our mission is to make property investment safer, faster and more accessible for everyone.

We’ve built an all-in-one property investment platform that supports investors from opportunity analysis and company formation through to financing, accounting and portfolio management. By bringing software, data and specialist services into one experience, we make property investing simpler, clearer and more cost-effective.

We’re now building the intelligence layer that will help investors understand opportunities, make better decisions and manage their portfolios. We bring together detailed knowledge of our customers’ investments, services such as mortgages, lettings and insurance, and a team that lives and breathes property.

We’re turning our property expertise into an intelligence layer that can scale. That starts with a data platform: selecting trusted sources, keeping information current and making it useful to our products and AI agents.

We’re looking for someone to own that foundation.

The opportunity

You’ll define and build the data platform that powers GetGround’s intelligence layer. This is a hands-on role with substantial architectural ownership: choosing how we ingest, structure, curate and serve data, while improving the foundations we already have.

The scope goes beyond integrating with APIs. You’ll build ways to ingest unstructured policy updates, regulatory guidance and published documents, turning them into reliable data our intelligence layer can use.

You’ll work closely with engineering, product and our property experts to turn domain knowledge into useful data. You’ll also design for international expansion, so entering each new market builds on a shared platform.

There’s an opportunity to influence how we build our data organisation over time, including the capabilities, standards and future hires we need.

What you’ll do

  • Own data as a product. Start with the decisions our customers and AI agents need to make, then work backwards to the data required. Judge success by the usefulness and reliability of what you enable.

  • Be opinionated about sources and quality. Work with our property experts to identify the most valuable datasets and assess their authority, coverage, freshness and limitations. Establish clear standards for what enters the platform and how conflicting information is handled.

  • Build ingestion beyond APIs. Develop reliable pipelines for structured datasets, external APIs, documents and published guidance. Ingest updates from sources such as HMRC and other relevant authorities, detecting changes promptly and turning them into usable, traceable data.

  • Make data usable by our intelligence layer. Structure and serve information so our products and AI agents can retrieve the right facts in context. Preserve source provenance, geographic scope and effective dates so consumers can distinguish current information from historical or superseded guidance.

  • Design for international expansion. Build shared models and ingestion patterns that accommodate differences in property markets, tax systems and regulation. When we expand geographies, we want to go at speed, without rebuilding the platform.

  • Own reliability throughout the lifecycle. Build monitoring, validation and recovery into ingestion, transformation, storage and serving. Know what is stale, missing or incorrect, understand the customer impact and address the root cause.

  • Set the technical direction and deliver it. Make clear trade-offs between immediate product needs and long-term architecture. Ship useful improvements early, document decisions and help shape the standards and future team needed to support the platform.

What you bring

  • Experience owning substantial data systems. You’ve designed, built and operated production data platforms or major parts of them, and can explain the architectural decisions you made and their consequences.

  • Strong engineering fundamentals. You bring strong SQL, data modelling and production programming skills, with practical experience in orchestration, testing, deployment and operating reliable pipelines.

  • Judgment about the data itself. You can evaluate whether a source is fit for a particular use, reconcile inconsistent information and make uncertainty or gaps visible to downstream consumers.

  • Experience with messy external sources. You’ve handled inconsistent formats, changing schemas, incomplete records, rate limits and integration failures. You’re comfortable working beyond clean, well-documented APIs.

  • A product mindset. You care about the decisions your data supports. You can work with domain experts and product engineers to translate an ambiguous need into a useful data product.

  • Architectural ownership. You can review an existing system, establish a direction and deliver improvements incrementally. You understand access controls, privacy and the responsibilities that come with combining customer and external data.

  • Clear communication and initiative. You surface problems early, write down decisions and challenge assumptions constructively. You’re comfortable making progress without a fully specified ticket.

Bonus

  • Experience building data foundations for AI products, including retrieval, document processing or evaluating the quality of information supplied to agents.

  • Experience modelling policy or regulatory information, including versioning and effective dates.

  • Experience with property, financial services, geospatial data or international datasets.

  • Familiarity with GCP, where we run our infrastructure, and experience working alongside backend engineering teams.

  • Experience establishing data standards or helping build a data team.

This role isn’t for you if

  • You just want to keep the pipelines running. You’ll need to care about which data we use, whether it can be trusted and how it improves the decisions our products support.

  • You want a fully specified architecture to implement. We need someone who can assess what exists, challenge assumptions and take ownership of the technical direction.

  • You only want to work with clean, structured data. Important information arrives through documents, policy announcements and inconsistent external sources. Making it usable is part of the job.

  • You want to stay removed from the product or domain. You’ll work closely with product engineers and property experts. Understanding what the data means and how it is used is essential.

  • You don’t connect with how we work. Our values—No BS, pursuit of excellence, feedback obsessed and healthy ego—mean communicating directly, holding a high bar, seeking feedback and being willing to change your mind.

Why join

  • Own a data platform central to GetGround’s next phase of product development.

  • Turn deep property expertise into intelligence that helps real investors.

  • Work on challenging problems across customer data, property information, AI and regulated services.

  • Shape the architecture for international expansion and help build our future data organisation.

  • Competitive salary and meaningful equity.

  • Hybrid London working, with three days per week in Waterloo.

  • Benefits include private health and dental cover, a learning budget, a home-office setup budget and 12 mental health days per year.

What we are building: The first end-to-end real estate investment offering - making the dream of owning real estate more accessible to everyone globally.

The Role

This is a hands-on, fully remote role in one of Plentific's cross-functional product engineering teams. The Senior Backend Engineer works alongside product managers, frontend engineers, quality engineers, and other backend engineers to build and operate the services behind repairs, quoting and invoicing, payments, contractor search, messaging, notifications, and fraud prevention. The role is open across the European countries where we currently employ or engage remote engineers.


Our backend is built primarily in Python and Django, with Django REST Framework and FastAPI supporting APIs in a service-oriented architecture deployed on AWS and Kubernetes. PostgreSQL, Redis, and Celery underpin data-intensive and asynchronous workflows. The systems handle complex permissions, legacy integrations, high transaction volumes, and business processes where reliability and data correctness matter.


AI-assisted, spec-driven development is part of normal engineering practice at Plentific. The Senior Backend Engineer turns product requirements into implementation-ready specifications, uses agentic coding tools across implementation, testing, review, and documentation, and remains accountable for the resulting software. AI-generated output is held to the same standard as human-written code. Success means delivering reliable services, improving the codebase and engineering practice around the role, and enabling the wider team to ship confidently at pace.

Key Responsibilities

Backend Engineering

  • Build and maintain APIs, microservices, and data pipelines using Python, Django, Django REST Framework, FastAPI, and related platform tooling.

  • Design service boundaries, API contracts, relational data models, and integration flows for complex property operations. Produce ERDs and other technical diagrams where they make relationships, ownership, and system behaviour easier to review.

  • Develop asynchronous and event-driven workflows using technologies such as Celery and Redis.

  • Write complex SQL, evolve PostgreSQL schemas safely, and optimise database performance where customer experience or operational throughput depends on it.

  • Review, refactor, and retire existing code so it remains readable, testable, maintainable, and suitable for new product requirements.

Quality, Reliability, and Operations

  • Write automated tests at the appropriate level and integrate them into CI/CD so changes can be released with clear evidence of quality.

  • Instrument services with logs, metrics, traces, and alerts that make production behaviour and failures easy to understand.

  • Diagnose and resolve production incidents across services, databases, queues, integrations, and infrastructure.

  • Design for security, resilience, performance, and data integrity across business-critical workflows.

Agentic and Spec-Driven Development

  • Use agentic coding tools such as Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, or equivalent to generate, refactor, test, review, and document code within clear technical constraints.

  • Evaluate AI-generated code critically for correctness, maintainability, security, performance, and fit with Plentific's architecture.

  • Break specifications into small, reviewable changes and validate each change against its intended behaviour before release.

  • Improve the team's spec-driven development practice through reusable patterns, review checklists, examples, and concise documentation.

Delivery and Collaboration

  • Collaborate with product managers, frontend engineers, quality engineers, and other backend engineers from problem framing through release and production operation.

  • Surface technical risks and trade-offs early, and propose pragmatic changes to scope, design, or delivery plans.

  • Review code and technical designs, setting a high bar while giving feedback that helps other engineers improve.

  • Coach mid-level and junior engineers through pairing, code review, debugging, and design discussion.

Requirements

  • Expert-level Python and Django, with strong object-oriented design and software engineering fundamentals.

  • Strong command of API design, service-oriented architecture, distributed systems, and asynchronous processing.

  • Expert-level relational data modelling, including the ability to produce clear ERDs, define entities, relationships, constraints, and ownership, and design PostgreSQL schemas that balance correctness, performance, and safe evolution.

  • Demonstrable ability to turn incomplete product requirements into clear technical solution designs for complex backend changes, identifying assumptions and resolving ambiguity with product and engineering colleagues through concise written analysis and appropriate architecture, sequence, data-flow, and entity-relationship diagrams.

  • Sound judgement around automated testing, observability, production reliability, security, and data integrity.

  • Strong working fluency with agentic coding tools and spec-driven development workflows, including specification writing, code generation, test generation, and critical review.

  • Clear written and verbal communication, with the ability to explain complex technical concepts and delivery risks in plain English.

  • High ambition and a strong sense of urgency, with the drive to deliver an ambitious product roadmap at pace using AI, and a positive, can-do attitude.

Experience and Qualifications

  • 6+ years of professional software engineering experience, with substantial commercial experience in Python and Django.

  • Experience building and operating Django-based services in production on AWS and Kubernetes.

  • Experience with Django REST Framework or FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Redis, Celery, and CI/CD pipelines.

  • Track record of designing and safely evolving complex relational data models in a large, long-lived production codebase, using ERDs and written technical designs to align engineers and stakeholders while preserving design quality, testability, maintainability, and safe evolution.

Senior Network Developer

About Share

Share is the global marketplace for bandwidth. We aggregate telco infrastructure across Africa (fiber routes, subsea capacity, data centers, cloud on-ramps) into a single intelligence layer. That lets ISPs, hyperscalers and AI companies get connectivity where they need it in seconds, not months.

Today, bandwidth is bought and sold through slow, private, one-off deals, with almost no price transparency. We're replacing that with one neutral exchange: an API on top of real infrastructure, with prices set by actual supply and demand. It's already live across East Africa, with thousands of kilometers of fiber, 12 infrastructure providers, 10 data centers, and around 8 million people served.

The Role

Our network is the foundation of the product. Every route a customer provisions through our API has to exist, perform and stay up on real hardware. We're hiring a Senior Network Developer to design and build that network as software: a distributed, multi-provider fabric that engineers change through code, not by logging into devices.

You'll own the network architecture end to end. That covers our BGP edge (transit, peering at KIXP and LINX, private interconnects with hyperscalers), the backbone, and the PoPs and data centers we're adding across the continent. You'll set the standards our network is built to, which partner ISPs connecting to us will inherit. As we grow, you'll also help build the network engineering team.

What you'll do

  • Design the backbone and PoP architecture as standard, repeatable building blocks, from edge to data center, so we can add capacity and new markets without redesigning each time.

  • Drive our move to Segment Routing and a clean IP architecture, including IPv4 reuse, IPv6, and how customer and internal address space coexist.

  • Build on disaggregated white-box hardware (Edgecore with IP Infusion OcNOS today), and make the hardware and software calls that keep us fast and affordable.

  • Turn operations into software. That means a source of truth (Nautobot), templated config (Jinja), and CI/CD with validation, staged rollouts and rollback for every change.

  • Build the telemetry and observability that show what the network is really doing. Use AI where it actually helps: anomaly detection, automated triage, and auto-remediation with a human in the loop.

  • Own availability. Limit how much any failure can affect, mitigate first and diagnose second, and turn post-mortems into fixes in the system.

  • Work with our software team on the API and provisioning layer that exposes the network to customers, and with partner ISPs' engineers on the hand-off.

  • Help hire and develop the engineers who'll run this with you.

Our Ideal Candidate

  • Hands-on with white-box or disaggregated networking, including choosing hardware and knowing where the silicon limits you.

  • You treat the network as code. You write automation yourself (Python or similar), and you've built or run the pipelines, source of truth and telemetry that make that safe.

  • Streaming telemetry (gNMI/gRPC, sFlow), and building your own monitoring tooling.

  • 400G/800G and optical (ZR) deployments, including vendor selection and certification.

  • Access networks (GPON/XGS-PON) and MikroTik or Huawei gear, since many partner ISPs run it.

  • Building networks in emerging markets such as Africa or Latin America.

  • DDoS mitigation at the edge.

If you don't tick every box but have built and run large networks in production, apply anyway.

jobs.title: Network Operation Engineer
jobs.description:
Network Operations Engineer

1. About the role

Share is the global marketplace for bandwidth. We aggregate telco infrastructure into a single layer and give ISPs, hyperscalers, and AI companies a clean path to deliver connectivity into every home and business across Kenya and the continent. Behind that marketplace is a real network: a BGP edge peering with Tier 1 transit, hyperscalers, and local exchanges, an MPLS backbone, aggregation and access gear, and the systems that watch all of it.

For the partners who run on us, the network is the product, and the NOC is where they feel it. A clean shift is a partner who never knew anything happened. That is the bar.

We are early and the team is small, so we cannot afford a pair of hands that only knows how to escalate. We need a capable network engineer who can stand a shift, resolve real faults without waking anyone, and then keep building the network while East Africa sleeps: propagation and peering checks, health passes across the estate, config changes through to merge, tickets off the board, automation that takes the next repetitive job off everyone's plate. The watching is the floor of this role, not the ceiling.

The NOC you would be joining is not a legacy one. We are building it as an AI assisted operations environment from the ground up. The forwarding plane runs on open source routing and forwarding software, every device configuration lives in Git, and an LLM layer sits on top of the live network state. When something moves, that layer reads the telemetry, correlates it against the topology and the config history, and puts a probable cause and a candidate fix in front of the engineer on shift. The point is not to replace your judgment. It is to collapse the time between an alert firing and you knowing where to look, so mean time to repair is measured in minutes.

You sit inside that system. You use it, you push back on it when it is wrong, and what you catch that it misses is part of how it gets smarter. As we build automation out across the NOC, you are not just a consumer of the tooling. You help write it.

2. What you'll do

Watch, and know what you're looking at. Sit on our monitoring stack (Zabbix and Grafana dashboards, flow telemetry, alerting) and actually read it. Learn what normal looks like so abnormal jumps out at you: a BGP session that dropped, a link that went down, latency climbing on a path, a capacity threshold breached, a partner suddenly pushing or pulling nothing.

Troubleshoot and resolve. This is where you earn your seat. Confirm the alert is real, gather the facts, and localise the fault: one peer or many, us or upstream, a real outage or a monitoring blip. The assistive layer surfaces a likely diagnosis and a suggested fix, the config history is right there in Git, and the runbooks are live. Your job is to read all of it critically, decide what is actually true, and close out what you can on your own. Every ticket you resolve yourself is one our senior people did not get pulled out of deep work, or out of bed, to deal with.

Keep the network healthy, not just alive. A quiet shift is not an idle one. Run the proactive passes: check that routes are propagating the way they should, that RPKI and filter chains are doing their job, that peering and transit sessions are clean across the edge, that no PoP is drifting toward a capacity wall. Catch the slow degradations that never trip an alert. The day team should inherit a network in a known good state.

Build and automate. The repetitive parts of this job should not stay repetitive. Write the scripts that turn a manual check into a scheduled one. Push our config automation forward (Jinja driven generation, NAPALM or NETCONF/gNMI against the devices) so changes ship from data, not from memory. When the assistive layer keeps missing the same thing, that is a candidate for automation, and you are well placed to build it during the hours nobody else is online.

Move the work forward. You are part of the network team, working the same board they do. Pick up tickets from the Linear queue, take config changes through review to merge, and keep our source of truth (Nautobot) accurate as the estate changes. Real work lands while East Africa is offline, so the team wakes up further ahead than they went to bed.

Report exactly what is happening. For everything you cannot or should not fix alone, the handoff has to be clean: what is wrong, where, since when, what is affected, whether it is getting worse, and what you have already tried. No guessing dressed up as fact. No "the internet is down." A clear, written incident note a senior engineer can act on the moment they open it, and a tidy handover to the East Africa team at the end of your shift.

Escalate well. Know the ladder cold: what you are cleared to touch, what you must not touch alone, and who to bring in for what. Escalating early on a genuine outage is good judgment. Sitting silently on a problem because you were unsure is the one thing that gets people out of bed angry. Handle what you can, raise the rest fast and clearly, and do not turn either dial too far.

3. Who we're looking for

A network engineer who can stand on their own through a shift, and who treats the quiet hours as time to build rather than time to wait. You will not be the most senior engineer on this team, and you do not need to be. The people you escalate to are CCIE level. What we need from you is independence and range: work a problem properly, resolve a fair share of it yourself, and use what is left of the shift to actually move the network forward. Pair that with clear reporting, sound judgment about when to bring in help, and the instinct to question a machine's suggestion rather than follow it blindly, and you are who we are looking for.

Must-have

  • Strong networking competence, held in your hands rather than on paper. CCNA and well beyond it. You understand TCP/IP, routing and switching, IP addressing and subnetting, DNS, DHCP, NAT, and how they behave when they go wrong.

  • Real troubleshooting instinct. Given a degraded link or a dropped session, you know where to look and what to rule out. You can read BGP session state, follow a path with ping and traceroute, and tell a local fault from an upstream one without waiting to be told.

  • Working BGP knowledge. Reading communities and route policy, spotting a flap or a leaky origin, understanding how transit, peering, and RPKI behave at the edge.

  • Comfortable on the gear and the CLI. Linux, network device CLIs, and dashboards are familiar ground. We run MikroTik (RouterOS) across the network and so do many partners, so RouterOS experience is a real plus.

  • Comfortable working with config in Git. Configuration lives in repos, not on devices. Reading a diff, understanding why a config changed, and proposing one yourself should not be foreign to you.

  • Some scripting, and the appetite to do more. Bash or Python, enough to automate the repetitive parts away and to grow into our config and automation pipelines. We are not hiring a button pusher.

  • Clear written English. You can describe a technical situation accurately and briefly so someone picking it up cold understands it instantly.

  • Calm under pressure and dependable. When the graphs go red you get more precise, not more panicked. You show up for every shift, alert and on time.

  • Located in New Zealand or a nearby time zone where covering our deep overnight maps onto your normal working day.

Nice-to-have

  • CCNP, or MikroTik MTCNA / MTCRE.

  • Prior NOC, ISP, or carrier operations experience.

  • Hands on with MPLS (L3VPN, EVPN) and the multi-tenant isolation a shared backbone needs.

  • Exposure to open source and white box routing or forwarding stacks (SONiC, IP Infusion OcNOS, FRR, or similar).

  • Network source of truth and automation tooling (Nautobot, NAPALM, Jinja config generation, NETCONF or gNMI).

  • Familiarity with a monitoring stack such as Zabbix, Grafana, Loki, or Prometheus, and with flow telemetry.

  • Working familiarity with FreeRADIUS, CoA and Disconnect flows, and how session control and accounting hook into the network.

  • Exposure to applying ML or AI in network operations: anomaly detection, predictive failure analysis, automated triage or remediation.

  • IPv6 and dual stack exposure, and internet exchange operations (looking glass and route server behaviour, IRR and RPKI hygiene).

4. What we offer

  • A seat inside a serious, very senior network team, with people who have deep service provider backgrounds and will sharpen you fast. You will see how a real carrier network behaves under live conditions.

  • A front row seat to how a network actually gets run in 2026. Open source forwarding, config as code, and an LLM layer doing real operational work. Not a slide about the future of network operations, but the environment you would work in every shift, and help build.

  • Real engineering, not just monitoring. The role is built so the quiet hours go into automation, propagation and health work, and tickets off the board. The path into deeper network engineering and automation work is the plan, not a vague someday.

  • Competitive salary and private health and wellness benefits, fully remote, in a mission driven, investor backed company building the backbone of Africa's next generation internet.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Robot Autonomy (Planning & Navigation)
jobs.description:
Our Mission

At Laelaps AI, we believe robotics is entering a transformative decade, much like the arrival of the internet. Advances in AI, cloud computing, and hardware are reshaping what autonomous systems can do. Our mission is to build the intelligent software that powers physical security in the real world - enabling robots and sensors to handle dangerous and critical tasks that humans shouldn't have to. By engineering the orchestration layer for intelligent security, we aim to create a world that is safer, more secure, and more resilient.

We're a strong founding team based in Zurich, backed by visionary investors and advisors. We are engineering the future of security today!

THE ROLE

As a Software Engineer on Robot Autonomy, you will make our robots navigate dependably across real customer sites. Our stack works. The gap between working and dependable is the whole job. Every new site tests how a robot understands its surroundings and chooses where to go: a ramp the planner avoids, a narrow passage that exposes a poor route, a gate that changes the map, a person who steps into the robot's path, or localization drift that builds over a long patrol. You treat those cases as the real navigation problem to solve, not as edge cases.

You'll shape the technical choices behind reliable navigation, from sensor selection, ground segmentation, and traversability estimation to predicting how people and vehicles move and planning safe, efficient routes around them. The system has to work day and night, in challenging weather, across different embodiments and changing site conditions. We measure success by whether the robot completes its patrol on a live site, not by how it performs in simulation.

WHAT YOU'LL WORK ON

  • Navigation and path-planning design: how robots represent traversable space, select routes, avoid obstacles, and reach goals across complex sites.

  • Sensor integration driven by navigation requirements, including what ground segmentation and traversability estimation need in day, night, and challenging weather.

  • Environment understanding: how the robot distinguishes ground from obstacles and estimates which terrain is safe and practical to traverse.

  • Behavior prediction: anticipate how people, vehicles, and other dynamic obstacles will move, and plan routes that stay safe and efficient around them.

  • Field reliability: reproduce failures from deployments, find the root cause, and fix it at the right layer, from sensor data and maps to costmaps, planners, and recovery behaviors.

  • Planning under imperfect localization: plans that stay useful when the state estimate drifts and the robot must execute routes in tight or dynamic environments, working with the rest of Robot Autonomy on localization and control.

  • Validation on real robots: logs, simulation, and repeatable field tests to verify that design choices and changes hold across routes, lighting, weather, and site layouts.

  • New autonomy capabilities: work with the engineers building the operator application and backend so operator requests and new robot capabilities rest on a sound navigation design.

  • The field feedback loop: work closely with forward-deployed engineers to turn site issues into bugs, design changes, and improvements to the navigation stack.

  • Regular site visits to build a practical understanding of how robots and sensors behave in real operating conditions.

WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR

We're looking for an engineer who has taken a robotics system from unreliable to dependable and takes ownership beyond individual tickets. You can explain why you made a navigation design choice and what it costs. When a robot takes a bad route, you can tell whether the planner, the map, the state estimate, or the robot's behavior is at fault, and you fix the right one. You are comfortable in the field and want to understand how robots behave in real customer environments.

YOUR BACKGROUND:

  • A Master's degree or PhD in mechanical engineering, computer science, robotics, electrical engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

  • Proven track record building and deploying navigation on ground mobile robots in the real world (3+ years or equivalent depth).

  • Hands-on experience with mobile robot navigation and path planning: route or local planning, static and dynamic obstacle avoidance, costmaps, or recovery behaviors.

  • Understanding of how mapping and localization affect navigation, and the ability to diagnose when a planning issue is actually caused by the map, the state estimate, or robot behavior.

  • Understanding of how lighting, weather, terrain, and sensor limitations affect perception and navigation, with experience developing or validating systems for demanding real-world conditions.

  • Hands-on experience with robotics sensors and hardware, especially LiDAR, IMUs, and cameras. You can investigate issues across software, networking, and hardware boundaries.

  • Experience testing and debugging navigation on physical robots using logs, visualization, simulation, and repeatable field tests.

  • Strong ROS 2, C++, and Python skills.

  • Clear communication of navigation and path-planning design choices and their trade-offs.

  • Willingness to visit customer sites regularly.

NICE TO HAVE:

  • Experience with legged robots or with more than one robot embodiment.

  • Experience with Nav2 or a comparable navigation framework.

  • Motion prediction or planning among people and vehicles, such as trajectory forecasting or socially aware navigation.

  • Terrain mapping and traversability methods: elevation mapping, learned traversability, or semantic segmentation for navigation.

  • Experience with night-time or all-weather sensing, such as thermal cameras or LiDAR in rain and fog.

  • Background in security, defence, or other safety-critical robotics deployments.

What We Offer

  • Ownership: you are able to ship products and deliver project end-to-end.

  • Mission: autonomous security that keeps people and critical sites safe, including in defence.

  • Career path: a ground-floor seat with real runway. Prove your value and you will not have barriers to grow.

  • Team: work directly with PhD-level co-founders in AI, Robotics, and Physics, alongside a strong (and fun) founding team.

  • Compensation: Competitive equity/salary package

  • Culture: International founding team that is serious about building but does not take itself too seriously.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Robot Autonomy (Localisation & State Estimation)
jobs.description:
Our Mission

At Laelaps AI, we believe robotics is entering a transformative decade, much like the arrival of the internet. Advances in AI, cloud computing, and hardware are reshaping what autonomous systems can do. Our mission is to build the intelligent software that powers physical security in the real world - enabling robots and sensors to handle dangerous and critical tasks that humans shouldn't have to. By engineering the orchestration layer for intelligent security, we aim to create a world that is safer, more secure, and more resilient.

We're a strong founding team based in Zurich, backed by visionary investors and advisors. We are engineering the future of security today!

THE ROLE

As a Software Engineer on Robot Autonomy, you will build and own the state estimation that tells our robots how they are moving and where they are. You'll fuse data from IMUs, cameras, LiDAR, GNSS, and platform-specific odometry into accurate, real-time estimates that support reliable autonomy day and night, across different robot platforms.

This is a builder's role first: you'll use the estimation methods and tools best suited to the problem, then do the engineering needed to make them work on real robots. Our robots operate in complex environments where terrain, weather, vibration, lighting, and sensor dropouts degrade measurements. We care less about novelty for its own sake and more about whether your systems perform reliably across platforms in the field.

WHAT YOU'LL WORK ON

  • Design and ship real-time estimators for position, orientation, velocity, and angular velocity across our robot platforms.

  • Fuse data from multiple sensors, handling noise, asynchronous measurements, calibration errors, changing sensor quality, and dropouts.

  • Develop estimation approaches suited to different platforms, including reusable components and interfaces that account for their distinct sensors and dynamics.

  • Improve localization and odometry in challenging conditions, including GNSS-denied environments and cases with degraded or intermittent sensing.

  • Integrate state estimation with perception, planning, and control so downstream systems receive reliable estimates and useful uncertainty information.

  • Investigate failures using logs, datasets, simulation, and field testing; identify root causes and verify that fixes improve performance on real robots.

  • Build evaluation and testing workflows that make estimator performance measurable and repeatable across robot types and operating conditions.

  • Work closely with the rest of Robot Autonomy and with forward-deployed engineers to turn deployment experience into improvements to the estimation stack.

WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR

We're looking for an engineer who has built or deployed state estimation systems for real robotic or autonomous platforms. You understand that estimator performance depends on the whole system: sensor behavior, calibration, timing, platform dynamics, and how autonomy uses the estimate.

You're comfortable choosing an approach based on the operational need, then making it robust through careful implementation, evaluation, and field validation. You measure success by whether robots operate reliably in the real world, not by algorithmic novelty alone.

YOUR BACKGROUND:

  • A Master's degree or PhD in mechanical engineering, computer science, robotics, electrical engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

  • Proven experience building or deploying state estimation, localization, or odometry systems for robots or autonomous systems (3+ years or equivalent depth).

  • Strong understanding of nonlinear state estimation, sensor fusion, Kalman filtering, and uncertainty representation.

  • Experience working with real sensor data and practical issues such as noise, calibration, synchronization, vibration, and data loss.

You will work with research, product, and customer-facing teams to ensure that our models are useful against real engineering standards — not only benchmark metrics.

  • Work with industrial customers to understand their simulation workflows and engineering priorities, define use cases and success criteria, and incorporate their feedback into model development and validation.

  • You have deep expertise in crashworthiness, solid mechanics, and structural mechanics, with substantial experience in industrial simulation workflows.

  • You have a Master’s degree or equivalent technical depth in mechanical engineering, aerospace engineering, civil/structural engineering, computational mechanics, applied physics, or a related field.

With built-in governance, auditability, and human oversight, Camunda gives enterprises the control they need to move AI from pilots to production — safely and at scale. Trusted by over 700 organizations worldwide, including 9 of top 10 US banks, Camunda helps enterprises boost operational efficiency, accelerate time-to-value, and deliver better customer experiences.

Fully remote and global, we are in the middle of something bigger: transforming into an AI-first organisation, built on our own platform. We use Agentic AI to automate, orchestrate intelligent processes, and elevate human contribution across every team.

Named GP Bullhound’s Top 100 Next Unicorn list, 2025 Great Place to Work certified. Visionary in 2025 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Business Orchestration and Automation Technologies. ranked 3rd in Flexa's 2026 Most Flexible Companies, We’re growing fast and looking for top talent to join our team. If you want meaningful work, visible impact and put something genuinely rare on your CV, keep reading.

About the role:

We're hiring a Senior Software Engineer, Quality to build the agentic layer of how Camunda tests its software.

We treat quality as an engineering discipline. We build test infrastructure the way we build our product — real design decisions, real trade-offs, real ownership. What's changing is how that work gets done: we're moving from hand-written test suites toward agents that design, generate, maintain and triage tests across the lifecycle. We need someone to build both the agents and the infrastructure that makes them dependable, and to help shape our Quality AI strategy.

You'll support product teams that ship features without dedicated QA. Your job is not to become their testing safety net. It's to build the tooling and practices that let builders own quality themselves — and to stay close enough to real features to know where that tooling breaks.

Camunda also ships AI capabilities in its own product, so the evaluation practice you build for agent-driven testing feeds directly into how we test non-deterministic features.

You'll join colleagues who live our FAITH values: Focus, Ambition, Integrity, Talent and Humor.

Curious about the kind of challenges you'll work on at Camunda? Watch this quick 30-minute talk from our engineers to learn more about the new Camunda Exporter and how we’re solving complex problems at scale

What You’ll Be Doing:

  •  Build and operate agents across the testing lifecycle — test design, generation, maintenance, execution and failure triage.

  • Own the infrastructure that makes agent-driven testing reliable: environments, test data, tool interfaces, guardrails, runtime and cost control.

  • Define how we measure agent output quality, so teams can trust results instead of hand-reviewing them.

  • Apply that evaluation practice to testing Camunda 8's own AI capabilities.

  • Work hands-on with new features as teams build them, enough to keep the tooling honest.

  • Raise the quality capability of teams — patterns, tooling, enablement. Success is what builders can do themselves, not the number of tests you wrote.

What You Bring:

  • Ability and/or willingness to use our product

  •  5+ years as a software engineer. You write production code daily and would be credible on a product team; quality is your domain, not a step down from development.

  • Production experience building test infrastructure, developer tooling or internal platforms that other engineers depend on — designed and owned, not just extended.

  • Hands-on work with LLMs or agent frameworks: prompt and context design, tool use, handling non-determinism, and evaluating output quality. This is the differentiator for the role.

  • Comfort with distributed systems and CI at scale. Camunda 8 is a process orchestration platform; testing it means reasoning about concurrency, state and timing.

  • The ability to drive adoption in teams that don't report to you. You've built something another team chose to use, and you know what to do when the first version isn't picked up.

 Nice-to-haves:

  • Experience evaluating or benchmarking LLM systems.

  • Open-source contribution experience.

  • Java, TypeScript or Python; Kubernetes and Helm.

  • Background in developer tooling or platform engineering.

Equity: We also offer equity (where applicable) through our Virtual Stock Option Plan (VSOP).

Benefits & Perks

We invest in your wellbeing, growth, and ability to connect, along with perks that support you no matter where you’re based. Our benefits are globally designed and locally delivered where applicable.

  • Remote & Flexible: Work from anywhere with the setup that suits you, home office budget, co-working space support, and flexible time off to recharge when you need it.

  • In Person Connection: We invest in meaningful face time through our Annual Kickoff (Vienna in 2025, Madrid in 2026!), team offsites, and Camundi Connection Budgets, including contributing to meetups while travelling,, and local gatherings with fellow Camundi.

  • Health & Wellbeing: Access locally tailored healthcare, Modern Health for global mental wellbeing, and our Live Well Lifestyle Spending Account (LSA), a flexible, global benefit that puts you in control of your whole life, not just work, from: staying active, to caring for family, exploring personal passions, meaningful experiences, and investing in your financial wellbeing. The Live Well program launches in 2026 and scales to €1,000 annually from 2027.

  • Financial Security: Retirement and pension plans (often with company contributions), plus life and disability insurance where relevant.

  • Professional Growth: Up to $/€/£1,000 per year for self-driven learning: courses, certifications, books, you decide!

AI in our hiring process: Camunda may use AI tools to aid the screening of applications and during the interview process. You can learn more here

”Everyone is welcome at Camunda” — it’s a celebrated component of our culture. We strive to create an inclusive environment that empowers our people. At Camunda, we honour diverse cultures and backgrounds and are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to gender, race, ethnicity, religion, belief, sexual orientation, age, disability or any other protected characteristics under applicable law. We are looking forward to your application!

Come join us and be part of Camunda’s incredible journey: Make an impact at a pivotal moment in our story!

jobs.description:
Senior Network Developer

About Share

Share is the global marketplace for bandwidth. We aggregate telco infrastructure across Africa (fiber routes, subsea capacity, data centers, cloud on-ramps) into a single intelligence layer. That lets ISPs, hyperscalers and AI companies get connectivity where they need it in seconds, not months.

Today, bandwidth is bought and sold through slow, private, one-off deals, with almost no price transparency. We're replacing that with one neutral exchange: an API on top of real infrastructure, with prices set by actual supply and demand. It's already live across East Africa, with thousands of kilometers of fiber, 12 infrastructure providers, 10 data centers, and around 8 million people served.

The Role

Our network is the foundation of the product. Every route a customer provisions through our API has to exist, perform and stay up on real hardware. We're hiring a Senior Network Developer to design and build that network as software: a distributed, multi-provider fabric that engineers change through code, not by logging into devices.

You'll own the network architecture end to end. That covers our BGP edge (transit, peering at KIXP and LINX, private interconnects with hyperscalers), the backbone, and the PoPs and data centers we're adding across the continent. You'll set the standards our network is built to, which partner ISPs connecting to us will inherit. As we grow, you'll also help build the network engineering team.

What you'll do

  • Design the backbone and PoP architecture as standard, repeatable building blocks, from edge to data center, so we can add capacity and new markets without redesigning each time.

  • Drive our move to Segment Routing and a clean IP architecture, including IPv4 reuse, IPv6, and how customer and internal address space coexist.

  • Build on disaggregated white-box hardware (Edgecore with IP Infusion OcNOS today), and make the hardware and software calls that keep us fast and affordable.

  • Turn operations into software. That means a source of truth (Nautobot), templated config (Jinja), and CI/CD with validation, staged rollouts and rollback for every change.

  • Build the telemetry and observability that show what the network is really doing. Use AI where it actually helps: anomaly detection, automated triage, and auto-remediation with a human in the loop.

  • Own availability. Limit how much any failure can affect, mitigate first and diagnose second, and turn post-mortems into fixes in the system.

  • Work with our software team on the API and provisioning layer that exposes the network to customers, and with partner ISPs' engineers on the hand-off.

  • Help hire and develop the engineers who'll run this with you.

Our Ideal Candidate

  • 8+ years building and operating large networks at a hyperscaler, CDN, internet exchange, carrier or ISP.

  • Deep BGP at scale: route policy, communities, RPKI, traffic engineering, peering and transit.

  • Strong data center and backbone design. You know Clos/EVPN-VXLAN fabrics and MPLS or Segment Routing, and when each makes sense.

  • Hands-on with white-box or disaggregated networking, including choosing hardware and knowing where the silicon limits you.

  • You treat the network as code. You write automation yourself (Python or similar), and you've built or run the pipelines, source of truth and telemetry that make that safe.

  • You've owned availability for something that couldn't go down, and can walk us through a real incident: what broke, how you found it, and what you changed.

  • AI-native in how you work. You've built with these tools, not just used them, and you have a view on where they help in operations and where they don't.

  • You think like an owner. You bring ideas, not tickets, and you want to help build a team, not just a network.

  • A clear, direct communicator who's comfortable with partners' engineers and with our founders.

Nice to have

  • Experience at an internet exchange, or running peering at scale.

  • Open networking stacks like SONiC, OcNOS or FRR, or contributions to them.

  • Streaming telemetry (gNMI/gRPC, sFlow), and building your own monitoring tooling.

  • 400G/800G and optical (ZR) deployments, including vendor selection and certification.

  • Access networks (GPON/XGS-PON) and MikroTik or Huawei gear, since many partner ISPs run it.

  • Building networks in emerging markets such as Africa or Latin America.

  • DDoS mitigation at the edge.

If you don't tick every box but have built and run large networks in production, apply anyway.

Compensation & Benefits

Competitive salary and meaningful equity in a venture-backed company (US-incorporated, with a Kenya operating entity)

jobs.title: Enseignante Chercheuse ou Enseignant Chercheur (Maître de conférences)  Qualité des Environnements Intérieurs en CDI à IMT Nord Europe
jobs.description:
INTITULÉ : « Qualité des Environnements Intérieurs ».

SPÉCIALITÉS : « Qualité de l'air intérieur, Physico-chimie de l'air, Performance énergétique et environnementale des bâtiments ».

ÉTABLISSEMENT D'AFFECTATION :

École Nationale Supérieure Mines-Télécom Lille Douai dont le nom d'usage est IMT Nord Europe.

Direction / Service : Centre d'Enseignement, de Recherche et d'Innovation Énergie Environnement (CERI EE)

Responsable hiérarchique : Directrice du CERI Énergie Environnement

Catégorie : Agent de catégorie A ou contractuel cadre de gestion de catégorie II

Nature du poste : CDI

Lieu de travail : Site de Douai. Des déplacements sur les autres sites de l'École sont à prévoir

CONTEXTE

École sous tutelle du ministère de l'économie, des finances et de la souveraineté industrielle et numérique, et école de l'Institut Mines Télécom, IMT Nord Europe a 3 missions principales : former des ingénieurs responsables aptes à résoudre les grandes problématiques du XXIème siècle ; mener des recherches débouchant sur des innovations à haute valeur ajoutée ; soutenir le développement des territoires notamment en facilitant l'innovation et les créations d'entreprises. Son objectif est de former les ingénieurs de demain, maîtrisant à la fois les technologies numériques et les savoir-faire industriels. Idéalement située au carrefour de l'Europe, à 1 heure de Paris, 30 minutes de Bruxelles et 1h30 de Londres, IMT Nord Europe a l'ambition de devenir un acteur majeur des grandes transformations industrielles, numériques et environnementales du XXIème siècle en combinant, tant dans ses enseignements et que dans sa recherche, les sciences de l'ingénieur et les technologies du digital.

Localisée sur 2 sites principaux d'enseignement et de recherche, à Lille et à Douai, IMT Nord Europe s'appuie sur plus de 20 000m² de laboratoire pour développer un enseignement de haut niveau et une recherche d'excellence dans les domaines suivants :

•      Énergie Environnement

•      Systèmes Numériques

•      Matériaux et Procédés

L'École dispose également d'antennes à Dunkerque, Valenciennes et Alençon.

Pour plus de détails, consulter le site internet de l'Ecole : www.imt-nord-europe.fr

Le poste est à pourvoir au sein du Centre d'Enseignement, de Recherche et d'Innovation Énergie Environnement (CERI EE) (https://recherche.imt-nord-europe.fr/energie-environnement-ceri/).

Le CERI EE développe des activités au cœur des transitions énergétiques et environnementales. Sa recherche est orientée vers les sciences de l'atmosphère, la qualité des environnements intérieurs et les enjeux de l'efficacité énergétique et de la décarbonation. Le CERI est structuré en trois axes thématiques : EFT (Énergie, Fluides et Transferts), OSPA (Observations, Sources et Processus physico-chimiques Atmosphériques) et QEI (Qualité des Environnements Intérieurs).

L'axe thématique QEI porte sur l'étude, l'identification et la caractérisation des sources de polluants dans les espaces clos et/ou confinés, l'analyse des interactions entre l'air intérieur et les matériaux, ainsi que l'étude de l'influence des environnements sur l'exposition et le bien-être des occupants. Les enjeux scientifiques traités couvrent plusieurs échelles, depuis l'intégration de matériaux et de systèmes énergétiques innovants jusqu'à leurs impacts sur les espaces intérieurs et leurs occupants. Dans un contexte marqué par le changement climatique et des exigences croissantes en termes de QEI et d'efficacité énergétique, une attention particulière est portée aux stratégies d'adaptation et d'atténuation, ainsi qu'aux rôles du comportement des occupants et des différentes sources d'exposition.

Ce poste vise à renforcer et développer l'axe thématique QEI au sein du CERI. La QEI intègre l'étude de multiples paramètres de confort (température, hygrométrie, bruit, luminosité) et de composition de l'air dans les environnements clos (logements, espaces de travail, transports, etc.), afin d'assurer bien-être et santé des occupants. Ces environnements doivent concilier les transitions environnementales et énergétiques avec la qualité de l'air et le confort des occupants.

L'ambition est de consolider le positionnement d'IMT Nord Europe dans ce domaine, avec une synergie entre recherche et formation. Il s'agit de renforcer un réseau de recherche et d'enseignement interdisciplinaire sur cette thématique en réponse à des attentes sociétales, des pouvoirs publics et des acteurs socio-économiques. Le recrutement s'effectue sur un projet de recherche et d'enseignement porté par un ou une titulaire de doctorat et s'inscrivant dans cette stratégie.

Dans ce cadre, IMT Nord Europe recrute un Enseignant Chercheur ou une Enseignante Chercheuse dont les missions sont décrites ci-après.

MISSIONS :

Sous l'autorité de la directrice du CERI EE, le ou la titulaire du poste participera aux activités d'enseignement, de recherche et de transfert de technologie :

Activités de recherche et de transfert de technologie :

Dans le cadre général de la stratégie scientifique précédemment décrite, les recherches auront pour objectif de développer des connaissances scientifiques et des outils avec pour finalité l'amélioration de la qualité de l'air des environnements intérieurs (en particulier mais de manière non exclusive dans les bâtiments), de la santé, du confort et de l'exposition des occupants tout en accompagnant les transformations du cadre bâti nécessaires à la transition écologique et énergétique.

Les thèmes de recherche attendus pourraient porter sur :

•      La préservation de la QEI face au changement climatique et à la nécessaire adaptation à ce changement ;

•      Les contributions des environnements intérieurs à l'exposition des occupants en intégrant les moyens d'évaluation et d'optimisation de l'exposition et du confort des occupants ;

•      Les impacts de la sobriété énergétique des systèmes énergétiques innovants et durables sur la QEI.

La personne recrutée devra :

•      Développer une activité de recherche de haut niveau dans le domaine de la QEI,

•      Initier, conduire et coordonner des projets de recherche régionaux, nationaux et à terme européens,

•      Développer des actions de recherche contractuelle et de transfert de technologie en partenariat avec des acteurs du monde socio-économique,

•      Créer des passerelles entre les axes thématiques du CERI EE et les autres CERI en lien avec les domaines d'excellence d'IMT Nord Europe et de l'Institut Mines Télécom,

•      Encadrer des doctorants, des post-doctorants et des étudiants de Master,

•      Préparer une Habilitation à Diriger des Recherches,

•      Participer au rayonnement de la thématique en lien étroit avec les autres collègues du CERI, notamment à l'international,

•      Publier dans les conférences et revues de référence du domaine, et participer à l'organisation d'événements scientifiques.

Activités d'enseignement :

Le CERI EE intervient dans l'ensemble des cursus Ingénieur. Il porte notamment deux des huit parcours de spécialité de l'école : GE (Génie Energétique) et GERI (Génie de l'Environnement et Risques Industriels) en formation initiale et une formation en apprentissage en Génie Energétique. Le CERI EE est également porteur de deux Mastères Spécialisés (MS) : le MS Bâtiment à Energie Positive, et le MS en Management des Risques Professionnels et Technologiques. Le CERI EE assure également des activités d'enseignements en formation continue, notamment en lien avec la QEI. Enfin, le CERI EE a pour projet de développer à court terme un projet de Master International « Engineering of Sustainable and Healthy Built Environment » dans lequel la personne recrutée viendra en appui aux personnes en charge du développement de cette formation.

La personne recrutée devra :

•      En lien avec le montage en cours d'un Master International Engineering of Sustainable and Healthy Built Environment, proposer un projet d'enseignement qui viendra, en partie, en appui des pilotes de ce Master pour notamment :

–     Contribuer à la finalisation pédagogique et à la promotion de cette nouvelle formation,

–     Contribuer aux enseignements et tutorats des étudiants du master. En s'appuyant sur l'alliance européenne EuLiST, ce Master vise à aligner activités de recherche et d'enseignement. Ces enseignements devront être dispensés en anglais.

•      Contribuer aux activités d'enseignement dans les différentes formations proposées à l'Ecole, dans son domaine de spécialité (QEI) et dans des domaines connexes (ex : chimie, thermodynamique, ...) en fonction de son champ disciplinaire ;

•      Contribuer aux activités pédagogiques sur l'ensemble des formations portées par IMT Nord Europe, en fonction de ses domaines d'expertise et des besoins pédagogiques ;

•      Contribuer à la mise en place d'innovations pédagogiques intégrant les outils numériques (MOOC, classe inversée, etc.),

•      S'investir dans les activités d'encadrement pédagogique (projets, stages, tutorats) et de sélection (concours).


PROFIL : (Prérequis/ Diplôme)

La personne retenue devra être titulaire d'un doctorat et justifier d'une expérience de recherche dans le domaine de la Qualité des Environnements Intérieurs ou dans une discipline contribuant à son étude, telle que la physico-chimie de l'air intérieur, l'évaluation de l'exposition individuelle, ou encore la performance énergétique et environnementale des bâtiments. Le profil recherché repose avant tout sur de solides compétences expérimentales, complété par une bonne compréhension des enjeux et des outils de simulation de la qualité de l'air intérieur. Ainsi, une aptitude à développer des recherches aux interfaces disciplinaires est recherchée afin d'articuler les problématiques d'exposition et de confort des occupants avec les caractéristiques des bâtiments et les stratégies d'amélioration de leur performance énergétique.

Il est attendu du candidat ou de la candidate de :

•      Démontrer une capacité à appréhender les enjeux multidisciplinaires liés à la QEI, avec une ouverture scientifique permettant d'intégrer des problématiques variées et de travailler aux interfaces disciplinaires ;

•      Faire preuve d'une aptitude à développer de nouvelles compétences dans des champs disciplinaires complémentaires à son profil initial ;

•      Posséder une bonne compréhension des enjeux industriels et sociétaux liés aux thématiques du poste ;

•      Attester d'une activité scientifique de qualité, traduite par des publications dans des revues et conférences à fort impact, idéalement en collaboration avec des équipes internationales ;

•      Présenter, si possible, une expérience dans le montage et la conduite de projets financés sur appels à projets compétitifs, avec obtention de financements externes ou démontrer une aptitude à coordonner des actions collectives ;

•      Montrer une appétence pour la transmission des connaissances et l'enseignement en démontrant si possible une expérience en termes d'innovations pédagogiques (MOOC, enseignement hybride, méthodes actives) ;

•      Faire preuve de compétences organisationnelles et relationnelles de manière à interagir efficacement avec l'ensemble des interlocuteurs (enseignement, recherche, support technique et autres partenaires industriels notamment) ;

•      Faire preuve d'autonomie, d'initiative, d'esprit collectif et d'un sens affirmé du service public ;

•      Disposer de solides compétences en communication scientifique et en vulgarisation, en français comme en anglais.

Une expérience internationale, une participation à des projets collaboratifs ainsi qu'un premier réseau au sein des communautés académiques et/ou industrielles constitueront des atouts appréciés. La préparation de l'HDR s'inscrira dans la perspective de l'évolution de carrière de la personne recrutée.

La résidence administrative est fixée à Douai. Des déplacements réguliers sont à prévoir sur l'ensemble des implantations de l'école notamment pour l'enseignement mais aussi de manière plus générale au national et à l'international dans le cadre des activités de recherche.
